title: QBR - Catalyst Systems - Health Check & Roadmap
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage growth, cost trends, reliability incidents in Q4, and roadmap alignment for upcoming model rollouts. Agreed to run a 2-week dedicated pilot to validate latency and cost improvements; Redwood to share SOC 2 + ISO docs and updated dedicated pricing tiers.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, good to see Catalyst folks. quick check, audio okay?
[00:06] Aisha Khan: Yep, can hear you Maya, thanks.
[00:09] Maya Patel: Great. This is Maya (AE), Carlos (SE) and Hannah (CSM) from Redwood. Today is the QBR / health check, we have around 45 minutes. We'll run through usage, cost, incidents, roadmap and then next steps.
[00:24] Tom Reynolds: Sounds good. From platform side I'll jump in on reliability stuff, Aisha I'll let you talk numbers.
[00:30] Aisha Khan: Sure. So quick context — since we onboarded in June we've seen steady usage uptick, promo-driven spikes in Oct. Our average tokens/day moved from ~1.2M to 2.9M, embeddings steady. The main pain is cost in peak windows and a couple of higher latencies during our nightly batch jobs.
[00:48] Carlos Ruiz: Got it. Do you know which routes/models those spikes map to? Are they generation heavy or embedding bulk jobs?
[00:55] Aisha Khan: Mostly generation for chat assistant and some large-batch embeddings for semantic search re-indexing. The batch runs at 2am and seems to overlap with other tenants causing queuing — we saw 250-600ms extra tail latency on a few nights.
[01:10] Priya Mehta: We also had a quick question about data retention; we want confirmation that logs/requests aren't stored longer than agreed and KMS is used for keying.
[01:18] Hannah Lee: We'll share the retention config we've set for your account — by default hosted logs are 30 days but we can adjust or move to private retention if needed. Also Redwood integrates with customer KMS for Private deployments, and Dedicated can be configured with your key policies.
[01:33] Tom Reynolds: For the latency — would moving to a dedicated pool help? We're balancing cost vs needing consistent P95 numbers for SLA.
[01:40] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, dedicated pools generally provide much more stable tail latency because you avoid noisy neighbor queuing. You also get predictable throughput. That said, cost per-token can be higher if utilization is low; we can model the commit tiers.
[01:53] Maya Patel: To add, Redwood Optimize has recommendations we can run to suggest batching thresholds and quantization profile by workload. For Catalyst's chat flow we think 4-bit quantized variants could reduce cost~25% without major quality loss.
[02:06] Aisha Khan: Wait, 4-bit? I'm worried about hallucinations. Have you seen quality regressions in internal tests?
[02:11] Carlos Ruiz: We do A/B evals — for many system prompts and short completion tasks quality delta is minimal. For your long-context summarization, we should run a small evaluation on your prompts. That's part of the pilot.
[02:24] Priya Mehta: On compliance — we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and confirmation of audit logs retention and SSO/SAML setup for console. Also curious about Private deployment options for EU data residency.
[02:34] Hannah Lee: We'll send the SOC 2 package and the PCI/ISO references. SSO via SAML is available now, RBAC support for per-team roles, and Private can be deployed in your VPC or in our on-prem bundle for air-gapped needs. For EU residency we have regions in eu-west that can be pinned.
[02:51] Tom Reynolds: There was also an incident on Nov 8 — a partial scaling failure that bumped latency for about 17 minutes. Can you walk through root cause?
[02:59] Carlos Ruiz: Sure. That incident was caused by an autoscaler mis-trigger when GPU health probes returned transient errors; it led to a short cold start while the scheduler rebalanced. We've since added probe backoffs and a keep-warm buffer to the Dedicated scheduler. I'll paste the runbook and incident timeline.
[03:16] Aisha Khan: Cool, we need the post-mortem for our internal auditors.
[03:19] Maya Patel: We'll send the post-mortem and the incident timeline; Carlos will add the mitigations.
[03:23] Tom Reynolds: On cost modeling, could you run a comparison: current hosted costs vs 3 levels of committed dedicated tiers (50%, 75%, 90% utilization)? We want to know break-even point.
[03:33] Maya Patel: Absolutely — we'll produce a spreadsheet with token/month forecasts, expected utilization and estimated committed price. We'll include the effect of quantization and batching savings.
[03:41] Aisha Khan: Another ask — can we test KV cache prefix caching? Our assistant uses lots of repeated prompts, maybe we can reduce token spend there.
[03:49] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, we can enable prefix caching and tune TTLs. For repeated conversational flows this is often a big win. We'll instrument token reduction per-route so you can see real savings.
[03:59] Priya Mehta: Also need to confirm encryption-at-rest for cached items and that keys are customer-managed.
[04:05] Hannah Lee: Confirmed — Dedicated and Private support CMKs. For hosted we can provide envelope encryption and rotate keys on a cadence.
[04:12] Aisha Khan: Great. Roadmap alignment — we plan to roll out a large search re-index in Jan, which will be embedding-heavy. We want an environment that won't blow the budget. If dedicated helps flatten cost, we're open.
[04:24] Maya Patel: For that workload, we recommend a temporary burst capacity option — Redwood Dedicated supports burst pools for scheduled heavy runs, or you can use a Reserved plus burst model. We'll include that in the pricing sheet.
[04:35] Tom Reynolds: For the pilot — can we do a 2-week dedicated pilot on a small pool and run the Jan re-index simulation against it?
[04:42] Carlos Ruiz: Yes, we can set up a pilot with synthetic load or replay your embedding job. We'll also enable extra telemetry so you can see token-level costs and per-route latency.
[04:52] Priya Mehta: Timelines — we need SOC2 docs and pricing by next Friday for budgeting.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll aim to share SOC2, pricing, incident PM, and a pilot plan by 2026-12-03.
[05:05] Aisha Khan: Awesome. Anything else?
[05:08] Maya Patel: Quick recap and next steps, then we'll close.
[05:11] Tom Reynolds: Thanks all.
[05:13] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

Set up 2-week dedicated pilot and pilot plan (Carlos) - kickoff by 2026-12-07
